instruction: QA rule: never name a top-level const after a built-in global (top, name, length, status)
input: An app's whole script failed with 'Identifier top has already been declared' even though the code looked fine. THREE loaded, but nothing ran. Why?
output: window.top, window.name, window.length, window.status and similar are EXISTING built-in globals. A top-level `const top = ...` in a classic script collides with them and throws 'Identifier ... has already been declared' at script instantiation — the ENTIRE script never runs (every other const stays in TDZ). Use descriptive names instead: `const crownTop`, `const pieceName`, `const listLength` — never the bare reserved word.

instruction: Fix the 3D solar system app (THREE.OrbitPath crash)
input: The app crashed with 'THREE.OrbitPath is not a constructor'. OrbitPath is not a real Three.js class. Fix it: load OrbitControls from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js, create controls with new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement), draw orbit rings with THREE.Line + BufferGeometry.setFromPoints of cos/sin points, store each planet's {distance, speed, angle} in userData, and advance angle in the animate loop.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
	<meta charset="UTF-8">
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
	<title>3D Solar System</title>
	<style>
		body { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; background: #000; }
		#canvas { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
	</style>
</head>
<body>
	<canvas id="canvas"></canvas>
	<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
	<script>
		const scene = new THREE.Scene();
		const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
		const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true });
		renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
		document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
		camera.position.set(0, 0, 100);
		const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
		controls.enableDamping = true;
		controls.dampingFactor = 0.05;
		scene.add(new THREE.AxesHelper(10));
		const planets = [];
		function addPlanet(name, color, radius, distance, speed) {
			const geometry = new THREE.SphereGeometry(radius, 32, 32);
			const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color, flatShading: true });
			const planet = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
			const orbit = new THREE.Line(
				new THREE.BufferGeometry().setFromPoints(
					Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, i) => {
						const a = (i / 64) * Math.PI * 2;
						return new THREE.Vector3(Math.cos(a) * distance, 0, Math.sin(a) * distance);
					})),
				new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({ color: 0x334466, transparent: true, opacity: 0.5 })
			);
			scene.add(orbit);
			planet.userData = { distance, speed, angle: Math.random() * Math.PI * 2 };
			planet.position.x = distance * Math.cos(planet.userData.angle);
			planet.position.y = 0;
			planet.position.z = distance * Math.sin(planet.userData.angle);
			scene.add(planet);
			planets.push(planet);
			return planet;
		}
		const sun = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffd5, emissive: 0xaaaaaa, roughness: 0.2, metalness: 0.8 }));
		sun.castShadow = true;
		scene.add(sun);
		const saturn = addPlanet('Saturn', 0x0080ff, 1, 15, 0.01);
		const rings = [];
		for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
			const ring = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TorusGeometry(5, 0.5, 32, 32), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x80ff80, flatShading: true }));
			ring.position.x = 14.5;
			ring.position.z = 0.5 * (2 * i - 1);
			rings.push(ring);
			scene.add(ring);
		}
		function animate() {
			requestAnimationFrame(animate);
			sun.rotation.y += 0.005;
			planets.forEach(p => {
				p.userData.angle += 0.002 * p.userData.speed;
				p.position.x = p.userData.distance * Math.cos(p.userData.angle);
				p.position.z = p.userData.distance * Math.sin(p.userData.angle);
			});
			controls.update();
			renderer.render(scene, camera);
		}
		animate();
	</script>
</body>
</html>

instruction: QA rule: template literals and script tags must close — never truncate output
input: An app's JS died with 'Unexpected end of input' because a backtick template literal was never closed. How do you avoid derailing?
output: 'Unexpected end of input' means the parser hit the end of the script inside an unclosed string/template/block. Guard rails: (1) every backtick ` opens AND closes a template — count them in pairs; (2) every <script> has a matching </script>; (3) every { has a matching }; (4) the file ends with </html>. If a section is too long, split it — never stop mid-string. One unclosed backtick kills the ENTIRE script.

output: Scene, Mesh, WebGLRenderer and PerspectiveCamera ship inside three.min.js. OrbitControls, PointerLockControls, TrackballControls and other controls are SEPARATE addon files. instruction: QA rule: a game app must be a game — rendering a scene is not enough
input: A 3D chess app renders a beautiful board and pieces with zero console errors, but clicking does nothing, there is no move function, no captures and no check detection, and the board spins by itself. Why is it still broken, and what must a chess app have?
output:
Rendering is the surface; the game is the logic. A chess app is only done when it actually plays:
  1. TWO sides of pieces (black AND white, 16 each, with correct colors)
  2. a click handler (Raycaster pick -> select a piece -> show legal moves -> click a destination to move)
  3. a move() that updates a real 8x8 board state, animates the piece, and handles captures (removing the victim)
  4. turn alternation, legal-move filtering, and check/checkmate detection
  5. a static board (the camera orbits, the board does not spin)
Verify by PLAYING the app, not just by watching it render.

instruction: QA rule: never create hundreds of thousands of objects — use InstancedMesh and few lights
input: An app built a city with nested loops over a 1000x1000 grid creating ~110k Box meshes and ~200k PointLights, then the browser tab crashed. What is the right approach?
output: Per-object Meshes and especially PointLights are expensive: a scene with 100k+ objects or thousands of lights will freeze or crash the GPU/software renderer. For repeated geometry use ONE InstancedMesh with per-instance transforms (setMatrixAt), and light the whole scene with 1-3 lights (ambient + a sun/directional or spotlight). Never add a light inside a build loop.

instruction: QA rule: only use THREE classes that exist in r128 — never invent APIs

output: No. THREE.ColorGradient does not exist in r128. Never call new THREE.<Anything>() unless you are sure it ships in three.min.js r128. Single-file HTML, Three.js r128 via CDN (global THREE + OrbitControls). A SINGLE detailed 3D rook chess piece STANDING UPRIGHT in the middle of the scene. COMPOSITION RULES — follow them exactly:
1. STACK the parts along the Y axis with explicit, non-overlapping y positions: base plinth (a flattened cylinder, e.g. radius 1.1, height 0.25) centered at y=-1.5 (spans -1.625..-1.375), tapered shaft (CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height) — radiusTop is FIRST, so a shaft narrow at top is CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.9, 1.4, 32)) centered at y=-0.6 (spans -1.3..0.1, seated on the plinth), a flared collar (radius 0.6, height 0.1) centered at y=0.3, and the crenellated top (radius 0.45, height 0.3) centered at y=0.6 (spans 0.45..0.75). REMEMBER: position.y is the CENTER of a part, NOT its bottom — compute it as (partTop + partBottom) / 2 so parts just touch.
2. The piece must STAND VERTICAL — do NOT rotate the group (no rotation.x set; keep the Y axis as the piece's long axis).
3. Battlements: exactly 5 small cylinders (radius 0.12, height 0.25) arranged in a RING around the top rim at a fixed radius (0.45) and fixed angles (i * 2*PI/5 for i in 0..4) — use a loop with trig, NEVER Math.random() for placement.
4. FRAMING: camera.position.set(3, 2.2, 5), camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0), controls.target.set(0, 0, 0) so the whole piece fills the middle of the frame.
5. LIGHTING — critical: a metal material (metalness >0.8) reflects almost NO diffuse, so a single weak light makes it render NEARLY BLACK. Use metalness 0.6-0.75, roughness ~0.3, a strong key light (PointLight intensity >= 2.5) PLUS a directional fill light from the opposite side PLUS an ambient >= 0x444444. Soft shadows, warm spotlight from the upper right, gentle slow auto-rotation of the piece, OrbitControls.
6. NAMING: never declare a top-level const named `top`, `name`, `length`, or `status` (built-in globals) — use descriptive names like `crownTop`.
7. No textures, no external assets. Two-script rule: when using THREE.OrbitControls you MUST load BOTH https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js before the app script.
output:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>3D Rook Chess Piece</title>
  <style>
    html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #111; }
    #scene { position: fixed; inset: 0; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <canvas id="scene"></canvas>
  <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js"></script>
  <script>
    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas: document.querySelector('#scene') });
    renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
    camera.position.set(2.6, 2.0, 4.2);
    camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0);
    controls.target.set(0, 0, 0);
    scene.background = new THREE.Color(0x4a4a4a);
    scene.fog = new THREE.Fog(0x4a4a4a, 20, 100);
    const ambient = new THREE.AmbientLight(0x444444);
    scene.add(ambient);
    const light = new THREE.PointLight(0xffffff, 2.5);
    light.position.set(5, 5, 5);
    scene.add(light);
    const fill = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.2);
    fill.position.set(-4, 3, -3);
    scene.add(fill);
    const rook = new THREE.Group();
    const base = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(1.1, 1.1, 0.25, 32);
    const baseMesh = new THREE.Mesh(base, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    baseMesh.position.y = -1.5;
    rook.add(baseMesh);
    const shaft = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.9, 1.4, 32);
    const shaftMesh = new THREE.Mesh(shaft, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    shaftMesh.position.y = -0.6;
    rook.add(shaftMesh);
    const collar = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.6, 0.6, 0.1, 32);
    const collarMesh = new THREE.Mesh(collar, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    collarMesh.position.y = 0.3;
    rook.add(collarMesh);
    const crown = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.45, 0.45, 0.3, 32);
    const topMesh = new THREE.Mesh(crown, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
    topMesh.position.y = 0.5;
    const battlements = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      const battlement = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.12, 0.12, 0.25, 32);
      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(battlement, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x777777, metalness: 0.7, roughness: 0.3 }));
      mesh.position.set(0.45 * Math.cos(i * 2 * Math.PI / 5), 0.28, 0.45 * Math.sin(i * 2 * Math.PI / 5));
      mesh.rotation.x = 0;
      battlements.push(mesh);
      topMesh.add(mesh);
    }
    topMesh.position.y = 0.6;
    rook.add(topMesh);
    scene.add(rook);
    const clock = new THREE.Clock();
    function animate() {
      const t = clock.getElapsedTime();
      rook.rotation.y = t * 0.1;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
      requestAnimationFrame(animate);
    }
    animate();
    window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
      camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
